newsitem.title: INDIA: Air India gets more seats to Australia.
newsitem.headline: Air India gets more seats to Australia.

text.p: Air India and Singapore Airlines Ltd have reached an agreement on additional traffic rights, Air India said in a statement on Saturday.

The higher capacity entitlements are linked to a code-share agreement by which Singapore Airlines will give Air India a block of seats on their daily flights to centres in the west coast of the U.S., Australia, New Zealand and Canada, it said.

The southern Indian city of Trivandrum has been given as an additional point of call to Singapore Airlines. Air India have got full traffic rights to fly to Southeast Asia, Australia and New Zealand, all transiting Singapore.
Each airline can raise capacity by 800 seats a week, each year for the next three years, it said.
Air India's limit of five B-747 transits through Singapore has been raised to six.
"Code-share agreements agreed between and Air India and Singapore Airlines will enable Air India to establish presence in new markets," the statement said.
The agreement was signed on Friday in Singapore by the two governments, it added.
